arxiv-2106-05743.title: Finite-Time Quantum Landauer Principle and Quantum Coherence
arxiv-2106-05743.creator: Tan Van Vu, Keiji Saito
arxiv-2106-05743.description: Abstract The Landauer principle states that any logically irreversible information processing must be accompanied by dissipation into the environment. In this study, we investigate the heat dissipation associated with finite-time information erasure and the effect of quantum coherence in such processes.

arxiv-2111-03495.title: Automated Supervised Feature Selection for Differentiated Patterns of Care
arxiv-2111-03495.creator: Catherine Wanjiru, William Ogallo, Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, Charles Wachira, Isaiah Onando Mulang’, Aisha Walcott-Bryant
arxiv-2111-03495.description: Abstract An automated feature selection pipeline was developed using several state-of-the-art feature selection techniques to select optimal features for Differentiating Patterns of Care (DPOC). The pipeline included three types of feature selection techniques; Filters, Wrappers and Embedded methods to select the top K features.

arxiv-2206-10038.description: Abstract The continued development of robots has enabled their wider usage in human surroundings. Robots are more trusted to make increasingly important decisions with potentially critical outcomes. Therefore, it is essential to consider the ethical principles under which robots operate.

arxiv-2212-02908.creator: Zhaoning Li, Qiaoli Jiang, Zhengming Wu, Anqi Liu, Haiyan Wu, Miner Huang, Kai Huang, and Yixuan Ku
arxiv-2212-02908.description: Abstract Autonomous cars are indispensable when humans go further down the hands-free route. Although existing literature highlights that the acceptance of the autonomous car will increase if it drives in a human-like manner, sparse research offers the naturalistic experience from a passenger’s seat perspective to examine the humanness of current autonomous cars.

arxiv-2301-11813.creator: Samuel Cahyawijaya, scahyawijaya@connect.ust.hk
arxiv-2301-11813.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Samuel Cahyawijaya, scahyawijaya@connect.ust.hk. Biomedical image reconstruction research has been developed for more than five decades, giving rise to various techniques such as central and filtered back projection. With the rise of deep learning technology, biomedical image reconstruction field has undergone a massive paradigm shift from analytical and iterative methods to deep learning methods To drive scientific discussion on advanced deep learning techniques for biomedical image reconstruction, a workshop focusing on deep biomedical image reconstruction, MLMIR, is introduced and is being held yearly since 2018.

arxiv-2408-08109.creator: Nihat Ahmadli, Mehmet Ali Sarsil, Onur Ergen
arxiv-2408-08109.description: Abstract Effective diabetes management relies heavily on the continuous monitoring of blood glucose levels, traditionally achieved through invasive and uncomfortable methods. While various non-invasive techniques have been explored—such as optical, microwave, and electrochemical approaches—none have effectively supplanted these invasive technologies due to issues related to complexity, accuracy, and cost.

arxiv-2510-18810.title: When LRP Diverges from Leave-One-Out in Transformers
arxiv-2510-18810.creator: Siqi Zeng ‡, Yao-Hung Hubert Tsai §, Makoto Yamada §, Han Zhao ‡
arxiv-2510-18810.description: Abstract Leave-One-Out (LOO) provides an intuitive measure of feature importance but is computationally prohibitive. While Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) offers a potentially efficient alternative, its axiomatic soundness in modern Transformers remains largely under-examined. In this work, we first show that the bilinear propagation rules used in recent advances of AttnLRP violate the implementation invariance axiom.

pmc-12614593.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing system is a powerful tool in plant genetic engineering; however, screening for Cas9-free edited plants remains complex and time-consuming. To address this limitation, we developed an RNA aptamer-assisted CRISPR/Cas9 system, termed 3WJ-4 × Bro/Cas9. In this system, the engineered RNA aptamer 3WJ-4 × Bro functions as a transcriptional reporter, serving as an alternative to traditional fluorescent proteins and thus avoiding their potential interference with Cas9 activity.

pmc-12733759.title: Association Between the Serum Creatinine to Cystatin C Ratio, Physical Activity, and Frailty in Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China: A Nationwide Cohort Study
pmc-12733759.creator: Kai Song, Chuanwen Yu, Yanwei You, Daniele Focosi
pmc-12733759.description: Background: Frailty is a major barrier to healthy ageing, yet early identification strategies remain limited. The serum creatinine-to-cystatin C ratio (sarcopenia index, SI) has emerged as a cost-effective biomarker of muscle mass and function, while physical activity (PA) is a key protective factor. However, their combined role in predicting frailty is unclear.

pmc-13228674.title: Exploratory analysis of infrapatellar fat pad MRI-based radiomics for detection of knee structure abnormalities in collegiate basketball players and swimmers
pmc-13228674.creator: Jack Consolini, Kevin M Koch, Alissa J Burge, Erwin Xia, Sharmila Majumdar, Garry E Gold, Hollis G Potter, Matthew F Koff
pmc-13228674.description: ObjectiveMagnetic resonance imaging (MRI) based radiomic evaluation of the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP) has been shown to predict knee osteoarthritis. As IPFP abnormalities can arise from sport-related injuries, this study evaluated whether qualitatively identified knee structure abnormalities in young athletes can be detected by IPFP MRI-based radiomics.

pmc-13249442.title: Worth the Wait? Comparison of Emergency Department Patients’ Waiting Room Tolerance for Real Patient Care vs Training/Simulation Scenarios
pmc-13249442.creator: Alice Rogan, Euan Watt, Stephanie Murphy, Emily Wheeler, Lisa Woods, Sagar Galwankar, Brad Peckler
pmc-13249442.description: IntroductionIn-situ simulation offers a realistic training environment with a higher level of fidelity compared to other simulation models. It is associated with enhanced knowledge retention and a higher level of composure during real clinical encounters. One common barrier to undertaking in-situ simulation is the concern that it contributes to a delay in providing patient care.

pmc-13470457.title: From probe to prodrug: immunoproteasome activity as a trigger for disease-selective therapeutics
pmc-13470457.creator: Cody A Loy, Yijun Gu, Samuel C Kim, Mariam V Mohagheghi, Noah B Trask, Marina Suarez-Pizarro, Lisa E Wagar, Claudia A Benavente, Darci J Trader
pmc-13470457.description: Developing novel strategies that can exploit a cell's endogenous machinery to selectively release toxic compounds in diseased cells, while leaving healthy cells unaffected, is a challenging task to accomplish. An established approach involves antigen recognition on tumor cells, enabling targeted delivery of prodrugs in which a cytotoxic compound is appended to an antibody by a cleavable linker.

pmc-13490514.title: Integrated five-stage cascade impactor with MIP-modified QCM sensor for real-time monitoring of airborne microorganisms
pmc-13490514.creator: Vahidreza Nafisi, Zahra Mousavian, Alireza Balaei, Yasamin Bide, Ensieh Fahimi Kashani
pmc-13490514.description: Pathogens present a significant threat to global public health, necessitating the development of rapid and reliable detection methodologies for effective monitoring and outbreak management. This study introduces a new sensing device that uses molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) for sensitive and specific Staphylococcus aureus detection.

pmc-13594085.title: Atlantic multidecadal oscillation modulates the impact of precipitation extremes on crop yields in Africa
pmc-13594085.creator: Haris Majeed, Carmen H. Logie, Daniyal Zuberi
pmc-13594085.description: Climate variability driven by North Atlantic sea surface temperatures variability through the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) is known to influence climate conditions in Africa. Yet, there is a need to understand whether AMO’s interannual variability modulates the risks of elevated precipitation on agriculture yields in regional Africa.

pmc-13599099.title: Single-session agreement of ChatGPT and Gemini treatment recommendations with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in thoracic oncology
pmc-13599099.creator: Kubra Hasimoglu Gurun, Fatmagul Cikladilmez, Guzin Demirag, Bahiddin Yilmaz
pmc-13599099.description: BackgroundTo evaluate the single-session agreement between treatment recommendations generated by ChatGPT and Gemini and real-world decisions made by a thoracic oncology multidisciplinary tumor board (MDTB).MethodsThis retrospective observational study included 102 thoracic oncology cases discussed at a university hospital MDTB between June and December 2025.

pmc-13644027.creator: Rupendra Nath Saha, Bhanu Duggal, Raghuraj Chawla, Akash Swain, Aditya S Agarwal
pmc-13644027.description: BackgroundCannabis use has been increasingly associated with acute coronary syndromes in young adults without conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
